# Day 3 – Logistic Regression & Classification Metrics

## Overview

Day 3 of Week 3 focused on **Logistic Regression**, the first classification algorithm introduced in the internship. The session covered binary classification, probability estimation, confusion matrices, and the most common evaluation metrics used to assess classification models.

## Topics Covered

- Logistic Regression Fundamentals
- Binary Classification
- Sigmoid Function
- Class Probabilities
- Prediction Thresholds
- Confusion Matrix
- Accuracy
- Precision
- Recall
- F1-Score
- AUC-ROC
- Classification Model Evaluation

## Practical Work

Completed hands-on exercises to:

- Load and prepare a classification dataset.
- Train a `LogisticRegression` model using Scikit-learn.
- Generate class predictions and prediction probabilities.
- Construct and interpret a confusion matrix.
- Evaluate the classifier using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and AUC-ROC.
- Compare evaluation metrics and understand their strengths and limitations.
- Document the complete workflow and analysis using Markdown cells.

## Technologies

- Python
- Pandas
- Scikit-learn
- NumPy
- Jupyter Notebook

## Learning Outcomes

After completing Day 3 I can:

- Explain the difference between regression and classification problems.
- Understand how Logistic Regression estimates class probabilities.
- Train and evaluate a Logistic Regression classifier using Scikit-learn.
- Interpret a confusion matrix and identify true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives.
- Evaluate classification models using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and AUC-ROC.
- Recognize why Accuracy alone may be misleading, especially when working with imbalanced datasets.
- Apply the standard Scikit-learn workflow to build and assess binary classification models.
